Yasmina Reza has successfully transformed the white Antrios painting into a trope, an extended metaphor for anything that stirs up uncomfortable and often destructive feelings between friends.
Bobby Cannavale, Neil Patrick Harris, and James Corden bring the star power, but that white canvas often takes center stage.
Art is entertaining middlebrow fare, a kind of Gallic update of the urbane comedy of manners that Neil Simon mastered in an earlier era.
Here, it plays more like a Broadway-branded luxury good: pleasurable enough, immaculately packaged, and priced according to the fame of its creators, not the weight of its ideas.
The play captures the meaninglessness of existence by making the experience of watching it feel meaningless too.

cn.t: Critics are divided on this starry revival: some find it a sharp, witty exploration of friendship with standout work from Corden, while others dismiss it as slight, dated, and overly reliant on celebrity casting over substance.
